entities.name: All India Trinamool Congress
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The All India Trinamool Congress (AITC or TMC), founded in 1998 by Mamata Banerjee — who broke from the Indian National Congress — is the dominant political party of West Bengal, the eastern Indian state with 90 million people, and represents the most successful challenge to the Communist Party of India (Marxist)'s 34-year stranglehold on West Bengal (1977-2011), one of the longest single-party runs in democratic Indian politics.

Mamata Banerjee (popularly called 'Didi' — elder sister) built TMC through fierce opposition to CPM's often violent political machine in West Bengal, becoming a symbol of resistance to Left Front dominance. Her party's 2011 victory ending CPM's 34-year rule was one of the most consequential electoral upsets in Indian state politics. Since 2011, Mamata has served as West Bengal's Chief Minister, fundamentally transforming the state's political landscape.

TMC has positioned itself as a regional alternative to both the Congress and the BJP — particularly significant as Prime Minister Modi's BJP has targeted West Bengal as a key expansion state. The 2021 West Bengal election became India's most high-profile state election in years, with a direct contest between Mamata's TMC and the BJP backed by Modi's personal campaigning; TMC won decisively, making Mamata one of the BJP's most formidable opponents nationally. TMC's identity combines Bengali cultural pride, welfare populism ('Duare Sarkar' welfare camps), and strong opposition to Hindu nationalism.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: All India Trinamool Congress — ending one of Indian democracy's longest single-party runs (CPM's 34 years in West Bengal), making Mamata Banerjee one of the BJP's most formidable opponents, and defining eastern India's political landscape — is one of the most consequential regional parties in contemporary Indian democracy.
